name: Technology, Nature and Society
description: We live in a time when technology is no longer experienced as a separate subsystem, but rather as a superstructure of society and life, permeating all of its existence.  Recent prevailing ideas of a strict separation between technology and nature or between the technical and the living have become obsolete. A variety of life processes are technically mediated (growth, propagation, movement, death, nutrition, etc.) and developments such as those of genetic engineering testify that nature itself has been transferred to a state of technical reproducibility. In this lecture series, the social negotiation processes of the relationship between technology, nature and society are analysed in a historical context and the consequences of the cultural specific demarcations for the scope of human action are discussed.
prerequisites: This lecture requires no specialist prior knowledge or experience
